Finite element discretization ​

In SpinDoctor, the finite element mesh generation is performed using an external package called Tetgen in 3D [2], and Triangle in 2D [19]. Each finite element mesh consists of

  • a list of nodes in three dimensions:   ;

  • a list of tetrahedral elements (  indices referencing the nodes).

The list of nodes includes double nodes that are placed at the interfaces between compartments connected by permeable membranes. This allows for representing discontinuous magnetization fields and (or and ) on the same boundary . To distinguish between the different compartments, let   with    for  . The set contains the indices of the nodes representing compartment , including interface nodes. In the adjacent compartments, the corresponding interface nodes will have different indices, distinct from .

In SpinDoctor, the finite element space is the space of compartment-wise continuous piecewise linear functions on tetrahedral elements in three dimensions. This space has a set of basis functions whose number is exactly the number of finite element nodes (including double nodes), and that are defined on the entire domain :

Let the finite element nodes be denoted by . The basis function ,  , is a piece-wise linear function, non-zero on the tetrahedra of that touch the node , and zero on all other tetrahedra (including tetrahedra of other compartments different than that do touch ). At the interface between two compartments, the value of is set to be the value it has inside its own compartment, distinct from that of the adjacent compartment. On a tetrahedron of that touches , is equal to on and it is equal to on the other 3 vertices of the tetrahedron. This completely describes the piece-wise linear function.
